gaps: FY2007-FY2013 (all fields): nothing published. Adyen was founded in 2006 and listed on Euronext Amsterdam in June 2018; the earliest consolidated financial statements it has published are the audited FY2015 statements, which carry FY2014 comparatives (June 2018 IPO prospectus). No annual report, results release or prospectus covering FY2007-FY2013 was found on the IR site.
FY2014 dilutedEPS: earnings per share is not presented in the FY2015 statements and the prospectus has no earlier EPS disclosure.
FY2015 dilutedEPS: not presented. The FY2015 and FY2016 statements in the prospectus contain no EPS note (the FY2017 statements, the first with an EPS note, show only FY2017 and FY2016).
FY2016 dilutedEPS: not presented in the FY2016 statements and no later opened document restates an FY2016 EPS.
FY2014 sharesOutstanding: the prospectus' historic share capital table starts at FY2015 (29,368,082 issued shares); no FY2014 share count is published.
FY2014 employees: no FTE figure is published for 2014; the prospectus' FTE-at-year-end table covers 2015-2017 only.
notes: All figures are IFRS as adopted by the EU, the only basis Adyen has ever reported on (its first published statements are the FY2015 statements with FY2014 comparatives). Amounts were read in EUR thousands and scaled to units; EUR is the reporting currency in every year.

revenue is the top line of the consolidated statement of comprehensive income as Adyen labels it: 'Revenue' for FY2014-FY2023 and 'Non-interest revenue' for FY2024-FY2025 (the same line renamed in AR2024). This is the gross measure that includes interchange and scheme fees that Adyen pays to issuers and networks and charges on to merchants. It is therefore NOT a like-for-like series across FY2023: Adyen stopped grossing up interchange from FY2023, so revenue falls from EUR 8,935,611k (FY2022) to EUR 1,863,406k (FY2023) on a change of presentation, not of business. Costs incurred from financial institutions fell from EUR 7,550,960k in FY2022 to EUR 147,811k in FY2023 for the same reason.

Adyen's own headline measure, 'net revenue' (Revenue less costs incurred from financial institutions and costs of goods sold; a line in the statement from the FY2017 statements onwards), in EUR thousands, is: FY2014 46,776 (not published - the FY2015 statements show only Revenues 153,675, costs incurred 106,552 and inventory change 347), FY2015 98,450, FY2016 157,985, FY2017 218,278, FY2018 348,913, FY2019 496,681, FY2020 684,200, FY2021 1,001,517, FY2022 1,330,166, FY2023 1,626,061, FY2024 1,996,074, FY2025 2,364,191. A revenue-growth chart built on this file's revenue field must either be split at FY2023 or use these net revenue figures; the growth story (18-46% a year) is only visible in net revenue.

operatingIncome is 'Income before net finance income and income taxes' (labelled 'Income before interest income, interest expense and income taxes' up to FY2019): after all operating expenses, before finance income/expense and other financial results. FY2016 includes a one-off EUR 56,282k 'Other gains and losses' (the Visa Europe share disposal), which is why FY2016 operating income (119,275k) is higher than FY2017 (93,465k) on flat growth.

netIncome and totalEquity are attributable to the owners of Adyen N.V.; the group has no non-controlling interests in any year, so both equal the statement totals ('Net income attributable to owners of Adyen N.V.', 'Total equity attributable to owners of Adyen N.V.').

totalDebt is the sum of the current and non-current IFRS 16 lease liabilities, the only interest-bearing debt Adyen has ever carried (no bank borrowings, no bonds, in any year). Leases first appear in FY2019, so totalDebt is 0 for FY2014-FY2018. Components in EUR thousands, non-current + current: 2019 50,903+10,791; 2020 118,051+13,434; 2021 119,968+22,996; 2022 169,873+33,200; 2023 172,397+50,666; 2024 173,321+54,935; 2025 183,269+69,097. This matches the Yahoo totalDebt in the snapshot (2022: EUR 203.1m vs USD 216.5m).

capex is 'Purchases of plant and equipment' from the cash flow statement, stored negative. Adyen reports capitalised software on a separate line ('Capitalization of intangible assets') and it is excluded here because the company does not report the two together: 2014 1,425; 2015 1,626; 2016 1,989; 2017 1,344; 2018 2,769; 2019 4,773; 2020 4,795; 2021 2,959; 2022 3,523; 2023 4,138; 2024 3,029; 2025 2,132 (EUR thousands). Yahoo's capex includes them, which accounts for the whole difference between the two capex series.

dividendPerShare is 0 (recorded, not null) in every year: Adyen has never paid a dividend. AR2025 note 37 and AR2023 note 35 state 'No dividend has been paid in the years presented', and the IPO prospectus says the board 'does not anticipate paying dividends'; net income is added to retained earnings.

employees is the number of FTEs at 31 December from note 4 ('FTE per office'), excluding contractors. It is FTE, not headcount: AR2025 puts headcount at 4,780 against 4,771 FTE and AR2024 at 4,354 against 4,345. Older reports' 'average FTE during the year' figures (e.g. 4,271 average in FY2024) are a different measure and were not used.

sharesOutstanding is the number of ordinary shares issued at 31 December, from the share capital note ('resulting in a total of N ordinary shares', nominal value EUR 0.01). There are no treasury shares. The count rises only through option exercises and share plans.

Restatements, latest figure used with restated: true: FY2015 operatingCashFlow was published as 137,903k in the FY2015 statements and restated to 138,398k in the FY2016 statements; FY2016 operatingCashFlow was published as 193,645k in the FY2016 statements and restated to 189,565k in the FY2017 statements (and 189.6 in the prospectus' selected-information table). No other restatement was found: the FY2023 figures in AR2024 are identical to AR2023, and the FY2017/FY2018 figures in AR2019 match AR2018.

Yahoo cross-check (snapshot-2026-10-26.json, USD, divided by the implied average EUR/USD rate): revenue 2022 USD 9,397,790,523 at 1.0517 = EUR 8,935.6m vs 8,935.6m here; 2023 USD 2,021,420,968 at 1.0848 = 1,863.4m vs 1,863.4m; 2024 USD 2,404,223,179 at 1.0803 = 2,225.6m vs 2,225.6m; 2025 USD 2,997,023,597 at 1.1323 = 2,646.9m vs 2,646.9m. netIncome: 2022 593,318,146/1.0517 = 564.1m vs 564.1m; 2023 757,539,008/1.0848 = 698.3m vs 698.3m; 2024 999,414,688/1.0803 = 925.1m vs 925.2m; 2025 1,203,074,957/1.1323 = 1,062.5m vs 1,062.5m. All four years agree within 0.05% using the same rates for revenue and net income, so there is no wrong-line, unit or scope difference - Yahoo's revenue is this same IFRS top line (its 'grossProfit' is Adyen's net revenue). The only trap is the FY2022/FY2023 break described above, which Yahoo's own series shows too (EUR 8.9bn then 1.9bn).

Document trail: the FY2014-FY2017 rows come from the audited consolidated statements in the June 2018 IPO prospectus (367 pp): FY2017 statements at F-18/F-19/F-21, FY2016 statements at F-68/F-69/F-71, FY2015 statements at F-113/F-114/F-116, with FTE at year end on printed p. 158 and the historic share capital table on p. 163. Those pages use embedded subset fonts that pdftotext returns as cipher text; the statements were decoded character by character against known plaintext to read the figures to the thousand.

The FY2018 annual report PDF served from the IR asset link is truncated (73 pages, ending inside the auditor's report), so FY2018 is taken from the AR2019 comparative columns, which cover every field used. The only value read from AR2018 is FY2017 diluted EPS (2.33) from its income statement on p. 65, because the prospectus' audited statements do not present EPS at all.
